chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, all together, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdul-Hamid Al-Taiy, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the testimony of the owned slave, he said: 'When he is just (adl), his testimony is valid. The first one to reject the testimony of the owned slave was Umar ibn Al-Khattab, and that is when a slave came to him regarding a testimony, so he said, 'If I establish the testimony, I fear for my self, and if I conceal it, I would sin with my Lord.' So he said, 'Give your testimony. Indeed, we will not validate the testimony of a slave after you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for an owned slave's testimony to be valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the testimony of an owned slave (mamluk) is legally valid provided he is 'adl' (just/upright), challenging the general Sunni practice of excluding slaves from testimony. It cites Umar ibn al-Khattab as the first to reject such testimony due to the specific fear of retaliation by the master, but clarifies that this was a contextual restriction for that individual rather than a permanent legal prohibition. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the moral integrity ('adalah') of the witness over their social status.
